title: Cheap whiskey and the rough boat voyage to Yokohama via Okinawa
summary: They stock up on $1.35 whiskey and sail a troop liberty ship through rough water at Okinawa, kept below deck for four days.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: -- we left Manila by boat. Before leaving, we were able to get our share of liquor. We could do that -- they brought some liquor in, we could go down and buy liquor, so we -- I stocked up with V.O. and I think it was only $1.35 a bottle. Real cheap, you know. That's what we got it for. And... I had some whiskey, just a man, I had one of the girls, she had two or three bottles for me, another girl had a bottle for me. And I did very little drinking, but I always got to have me some whisky on hand, you know. You never can tell when you might need it to bargain with.
And we went by boat to Yokahama, by the way of -- what's the island?
And it really was a prisoner ship. It was a troop travelling liberty ship, but it had been used to haul Japanese prisoners.

Uh-huh. Now, let me tell you one thing. After we -- we had a nice trip, all the way up. The sea was calm and nice. We get to Okinawa. It was a little rough out in the harbor. We told you about the harbor there. And I was downstairs in front of the boat. I guess that's aft --
On the bow. And that boat -- when we got in that rough water, that boat would go up like this, and

you could hear the rivets screwing, I mean, the rivets was moving in that boat, making noise. And that boat would go up in the air like that, you know. And it would 'ka-choong,' it'd almost throw you out of the bed.

And for four days, you weren't allowed upstairs, on deck. Man, that's a heck of a feeling, man. Tobbe down in that boat. And just think, any minute, the man might have to sound an SOS. And when we did get to Yokihama, they announced that if the boat had gone over -- I forget how many --
They would have to call out.

(Unintelligible) Because the boat would go over and lean, it would lean to your left, then it would lean to the right, see. Then she would ra'r back. And when she would go down in front, the rear end would come up. The propellor would be up out of the water.
